item.title: Burnham not considering public inquiry into UK activities of Jeffrey Epstein
item.summary: Victims’ minister said earlier that PM was ‘looking into’ inquiry into Epstein and another into Mohamed Al Fayed Andy Burnham is not actively considering a public inquiry into the actions of the paedophile financier Jeffrey Epstein in the UK, despite claims to the contrary, it is understood. The victims’ minister, Alex Davies-Jones, said on Tuesday had the prime minister had agreed to meet Epstein’s victims, was “looking into” an inquiry and was “taking this very seriously”. A separate inquiry into the alleged actions of the former Harrods owner Mohamed Al Fayed is also being considered. But the Guardian understands a public inquiry is not being actively considered by No 10. Continue reading...
